cells.tense: The work is here, in your hands, and it is holding.
cells.ask: Choose one thing you've been circling and give it a full hour of unhurried work, then stop while it's still good.
cells.core: You're not just thinking about the thing anymore. There's a method you've built and you're inside it — questions that get asked in the right order, answers that get tested before they're trusted. Maybe the best part is what it looks like when it's going well: the work gets quieter, not louder, and you're still in it. Right now it's steady. You can pick something up and finish it without the whole engine shaking. The hour after it is still yours.\n\nThe next piece is keeping the balance without turning it into a rule. The method works because it's yours, not because it's perfect. So take one thing you've been circling and give it a full hour of unhurried work. Then put it down while it still feels good, before the fourth or fifth pass, and let that be enough for today.
cells.sheetLine: Your method is holding. Let the hour after work stay yours.
cells.verb: working a thing until it holds
cells.place: the open room before anything has been chosen

cells.tense: You are bracing for a future where the work has to be finished before it can begin.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you've been rehearsing and do the worst, quickest version now, then leave it alone until tomorrow.
cells.core: You're running the whole thing in advance. Before anything is picked, the method is already there, testing futures that haven't happened, scanning for the mistake that will make it not count. Somewhere ahead is the version where the work is finished and proven, and you're living in that version, which means nothing here is allowed to be rough yet. This could look like rigor from the outside. From inside it's pressure.\n\nThe way through isn't more discipline. It's letting one thing be finished and unproven. Pick something you've been rehearsing and do the worst, quickest version now. Then leave it alone until tomorrow. Whatever it turns out to be, that's the one you'll have to beat later, and that's fine. Speed is not a betrayal of the method.

cells.tense: You are still standing at the door where you stopped starting things.
cells.ask: Name one small thing you've wanted to try and do it at the smallest possible size this week, badly, with no plan to continue.
cells.core: The tools are there. You know how to work, how to check, how to sit with something until it's clear. What stopped is the starting. Maybe a while back you picked something up and it didn't go, and you set it down and haven't picked anything up since, and now the room feels like a room you used to work in. The skill didn't leave. It just isn't being asked to do anything.\n\nThe way out isn't a big project. It's one small thing you've wanted to try. Do it at the smallest possible size this week. Badly. With no plan to continue. If it turns out to be good, you'll know where to find it. If not, you've at least moved the moment from before to after, and the door is behind you either way.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped starting. Try one small thing badly this week.

cells.tense: The pen is moving and you are calling it somebody else's hand.
cells.ask: Name one piece of work you did this week and say aloud that you made it, even if it was small and even if you had help.
cells.core: You're already working a method — asking the right question first, checking before trusting, not moving until the thing is clear. But you describe it as the project's requirement or the team's habit or just how the thing has to be done. Somebody else's discipline, borrowed. Meanwhile it's running in your decisions and getting them right.\n\nSometimes what shows up is that when it works, it looks like your judgment rather than a rule you followed. Somewhere in the last few days you made one small call and it held. Say aloud that you made it. Not the process, not the requirement — the pick. That's the ownership that's been going unclaimed, and it was yours the whole time.
cells.sheetLine: You made the call. Stop crediting the method.

attempts.check: The claim the record doesn't support is that Potential can only be expressed through method, when the seat is really about the moment before any method has been chosen. A reader could reasonably say that in their life the lack isn't discipline but the fact that nothing has been selected yet, so a method would be premature. The ask survives being wrong because it is an act of selecting one thing and staying with it for a short, fixed time, which is useful whether the diagnosis is correct or not, and does not require money, a safe person or a free schedule. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is any line about the seed containing everything, which is beautiful and unactionable, so every cell stays with the concrete move instead.
